transcript.text: the door on our built in dishwasher just crashes down when you open it now, used to stay put. Hotpoint I think

A dishwasher door that crashes down usually means the mechanism that holds it up—typically gas springs or steel cables inside the hinges—has lost tension or broken. This is a common wear item on built-in dishwashers after several years of use. Before we look at that, please check that nothing in your cutlery basket or racks is sticking out and blocking the door's path, and ensure the door closes squarely without hitting the worktop above it.
Nothing's blocking it, the door closes and latches fine and sits square. It just drops open with no resistance now. I heard a twang noise last week when it went.

That 'twang' suggests the internal tension mechanism has snapped. On Hotpoint dishwashers, this is almost always a failed gas spring (strut) inside the hinge assembly or a broken steel support cable. Because these parts are under significant mechanical tension and require removing the door from its mounting to replace safely, this is not an owner-safe repair. You will need to call an engineer to fit new hinges or struts.

candidates: Worn door balance springs or hinge cables (high)
Misaligned door or obstruction in the rack (medium)
